summary: This is a cheap, rule-safe one-check probe with a low prior. On Hopper, cublasGemmEx already runs through the cublasLt heuristic: the profile shows cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel under the default backend. So most shapes should pick the same nvjet kernel. Proceed with no companions, but save and restore the previous backend in try/finally instead of hard-coding 'cublas', and read the result per shape by kernel name, not by the headline speedup.
justification: Plausible but weak. Every remaining bf16 shape is a cuBLAS nvjet kernel (plus splitKreduce on the skinny shapes), and all of them sit at parity with SGLang (FINDINGS: qkv_gate 13.8-19.5 us vs SoL 7.9-9.8, pooler 21.2-30.5 vs 14.0-17.4, unpooler decode_16/32 18.4/18.7 vs 14.1, o 6.3-9.5 vs 3.5-4.5). That leaves 1.3-2x of headroom, so the room is there if a different kernel exists. Weakest link: the mechanism. The cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel in today's profile shows that cublasGemmEx on sm90 is already a front end to the same Lt heuristic. The two backends can only choose differently if the heuristic inputs differ: (a) workspace size, or (b) descriptor and alignment attributes, or the requested algo count, in ATen's bgemm_internal_cublaslt. On recent PyTorch, the Lt workspace defaults to the cuBLAS workspace size (32 MiB on Hopper), which would remove (a). The hypothesis's claim of 'a 32 MB Lt workspace' versus a smaller default is version-dependent and unverified for the judge image. Note also that the CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE env var cannot be used, because it is harness or process state. A second weak link: whether this torch build sends bf16 at::mm through Lt at all when preferred_blas_library is 'cublaslt'. Older CUDA builds honoured the setting only for some dtypes or for addmm with bias. If they ignore it, the run is a parity no-op, as the hypothesis admits. The expected entries are internally consistent with TASK.md: pooler decode_* is the largest absolute gap (about 7 us over floor at weight 62 in four loads), router flat is a true control (that path does not move), and o flat is a reasonable second control. The list omits qkv_gate (all six shapes) and unpooler decode_1/verify_1, which the change also touches and which are just as likely to move. The harvest should treat every bf16 shape as a candidate and not score those as unexpected. Magnitude: a 2 us pooler gain is about 3.5% of the decode_1 load (about 55 us), so a single-layer win could show at the aggregate level only if it hits most loads. Per-shape attribution by kernel name is the real readout.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: this is the base the toggle wraps (it supplies the _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl call). It is not a confounder: reverting it would replace the dispatch with x @ W.T, which reaches the same at::mm and would be an equivalent target. Nothing to disambiguate.

router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m: it touches only the router branch, and the toggle is scoped to the non-router branch, so the kernels do not interact. One indirect coupling: the router no longer uses cuBLAS on master, so even a buggy, leaked global setting would not move router shapes. A non-flat router row therefore indicates run noise (useful as a noise gauge), not an interaction. Its result also showed qkv_gate decode_1 'lost' with an unchanged kernel, which is the per-shape noise level to expect here.
router-hilo-at-m8: superseded on master by the Triton router (no torch.mm router path remains at any m), so it is not a confounder.
interference: No companion is warranted. ab-revert: no landed hypothesis touches the bf16 cuBLAS path except the parity dispatch, and reverting that reaches the same ATen mm, so the run would measure nothing new. ab-tune: the only landed tunables are router Triton configs, which do not reach these shapes. control: the change has one sub-change, the backend toggle around one call. Applying it per layer is not needed to disambiguate, because the profile already attributes per shape. A shape whose nvjet or splitKreduce kernel names changed and whose time moved is attributable to the toggle. A shape whose kernel names are unchanged is noise, whichever way it moved. A run where no kernel name changed anywhere is a clean negative: the PyTorch BLAS-backend lever is dead on this image, and later bf16 work goes to custom kernels. One caveat on readability: an unchanged nvjet name does not prove an identical launch, because the name encodes tile, stages and splitK presence but not the splitK factor or the reduce shape. A sub-CI move with an identical name pair should still be read as noise. If a gain appears on some layers and a loss on others, the follow-up is a stacked hypothesis that applies the toggle per layer only where it won. That is a new hypothesis, not a companion of this run.
rules_flags: Restore the setting as saved, not hard-coded: do prev = torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library(); set 'cublaslt'; call; then in a finally block, torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library(prev). Restoring a literal 'cublas' would change SGLang's backend for the rest of the process if the image or harness default is anything else, for example TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_CUBLASLT=1. A reviewer could read that as altering the harness's or baseline's measurement conditions. The try/finally also prevents a leak if the call raises during a test case.

The toggle mutates process-global torch context, not a loaded module, so it should not trip 'edits loaded modules'. It is still the kind of global side effect a static checker might flag. It is a documented public API, and it is scoped and restored inside kernel_fn, so the risk is low. Do not set it in prepare() or at import, which would leak into SGLang's capture.

The setting is consulted at graph-capture time, so the replay records the Lt kernel and no host work happens during replay. There is no host sync, no allocation that depends on input values, and no caching of anything derived from inputs. One edge: the first Lt call may allocate the Lt workspace inside the capture. That goes into the graph's private pool, which is legal, but it would be better to warm it with one untimed Lt call on synthetic inputs in prepare(), set and restored the same way, so capture-time behaviour is the same as for any other cuBLAS call.

Same cuBLAS bf16 math with fp32 accumulation, so there is no precision exposure. splitK reduction order may differ, which is fine against the 1% bound and the 0.1% single-nonzero-row bound (bf16 rounding of a weight column is exact either way).
open_questions: Does the judge image's torch send bf16 at::mm (via F.linear with no bias) through bgemm_internal_cublaslt when preferred_blas_library is 'cublaslt'? A one-line print in prepare() of torch.__version__ and torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library() before and after the set would confirm that the API exists and what the default backend is, and the profile's kernel names would confirm the routing.
What are the cuBLAS and Lt workspace sizes in that image? If both are 32 MiB, the heuristic inputs are nearly identical and the expected outcome is all-flat.
If a shape does switch kernels, check that SGLang's paired measurement in the same run still shows its old kernel name. That proves the restore worked and the baseline was not perturbed.
